t: The Spectator is a weekly British political and cultural magazine. First published in July 1828, it is the oldest surviving magazine in the world. It leans politically conservative and covers politics and culture, with pages on books, music, opera, film and television. Over its history it has had several owners. Meredith Townsend and Richard Holt Hutton were joint editors until 1887, and Townsend wrote most of the political articles. Later owners included John Strachey, Evelyn Wrench, the politician Ian Gilmour and the businessman Henry Keswick.
